records.name: Muhibbah Dinners
records.summary: A yearly communal dinner in Philadelphia where several chefs cook one shared menu. Proceeds go to local groups that serve immigrant and refugee families.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket or donation option for the dinner, eat the meal, and learn the menu on the night. Volunteers join the crew that helps run each dinner, and the group sends volunteer roles to its mailing list.

schedule.text: One dinner a year, cooked by several chefs.

cost.text: Tickets are sold as donations of $25, $50 or $100 to the partner charity. Check the tickets page for the current dinner.

first_step.how: When the next dinner is announced, buy a ticket from the tickets page on the group's website, or join the mailing list to hear about it sooner.
first_step.basis: Open to the public by ticket or donation with no membership needed, but the site shows no date or venue for the next dinner.
first_step.what_to_expect: The dinner is one shared meal cooked by several chefs, and the menu stays secret until the night. The tickets page sells $25, $50 and $100 donation options to the partner charity. Volunteers form the crew that helps the dinner run.
first_visit_tips: Join the mailing list, or follow the group on Instagram at @muhibbahdinners or on Facebook, so you hear when the next dinner is announced.
Plan on a donation of $25, $50 or $100 when you buy through the tickets page.
Ask the group about seating and access before you buy, since the site does not say.

records.notes: Tier 1 said proceeds go to immigrant legal aid. The current site names no charity on the tickets page (it says only partnered charity), and the homepage named Puentes de Salud, a health nonprofit, for the February 16, 2026 dinner. Summary changed to match. The homepage still shows the February 2026 dinner as the next one and gives no date for a new one; status is active only because that dinner is within 12 months. Venue for the February 2026 dinner was BLDG39 at the Arsenal (no street address on the site). Volunteer roles, time commitment and minimum age are not on the volunteer page. Puentes de Salud is a named partner with no link on the page read, so it is not logged as a lead.

records.name: Music Theatre Philly
records.summary: A nonprofit theater school for ages 2 and up that teaches singing, acting, and dance. It also runs an adult choir, adult dance classes, and productions for students and adults.
records.what_you_do: Take a class in singing, acting, dance, or art, or book a private lesson. Each class ends with a short showcase, and young performers can join a production; actors are cast at the first rehearsal.

schedule.text: Most classes run in 14-week sessions, one hour a week. Adult choir meets Thursday evenings and adult dance meets Tuesday evenings.

cost.text: Adult classes cost $350 for a full session, and adult dance has a $30 drop-in price. Children's class fees are not shown on the pages read. The site mentions scholarships and payment plans, which are arranged by email.

first_step.how: Choose an age group on the Find Your Fit page, then call 445-223-2683 to ask which class to start with.
first_step.basis: The Find Your Fit page says the classes suit people with no stage experience, and adult dance has a $30 drop-in option.
first_step.what_to_expect: Classes meet once a week for about an hour, in groups of 3 to 15, and each ends with a short showcase. Adult dance meets on Tuesday evenings and charges $30 a visit or $350 for a full session. The site does not say how a first class is booked, so call or email the studio first.
first_visit_tips: Mention your age or experience when you call, since the class list is split by age and grade.
Ask about scholarships or payment plans by email before you sign up, because the site points there for both.
Read the studio policy on registration and cancellations, which the site links to.
The studio is at 1301 Locust Street, zip 19107. The site does not give transit or parking details.

records.notes: Adult offerings from the adult classes page: Voices of MTP adult choir (ages 18 and up, Thursdays 6:30 to 8:30 pm, $350); adult dance (ages 18 and up, Tuesdays 7:30 to 8:30 pm, $350 full session or $30 drop-in); MTP Players production The Wedding Singer (ages 21 and up, $495). Session dates on that page carry the year 2026 and are used for last_sign_of_life. A search snippet listed children's class prices, but no fetched page confirmed them, so they are not recorded. The /classes and /spring-ages-2-5 paths returned 404; the Find Your Fit page was reached through the site search. The Playhouse is a separate play space for children 0 to 5 with a membership or day pass, not a class. Trial class: not stated on the pages read.

records.name: Musicopia
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that brings music and dance to schools and neighborhoods through workshops, short residencies, lessons, and student ensembles. It also runs a volunteer program for people 16 and older.
records.what_you_do: Schools and partners host its workshops and residencies, and it offers lessons and student ensembles. Volunteers can help at events, repair or move donated instruments, do office and photo work, or help the Musicopia String Orchestra.

schedule.text: Programs are set up with schools and partners. No public class schedule is listed.

cost.text: No prices are published on the site.

first_step.how: Fill in the online volunteer form at musicopia.org/volunteer after reading the Volunteer Handbook.
first_step.basis: Volunteers must be 16 or older and clear background checks before in-person work, and most programs run through schools and partners, so the public way in is a form or a staff contact.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical visit. Joining as a volunteer means an online form, a handbook to read, and clearance checks before any in-person shift. Roles include event help, thank-you calls, instrument repair or transport, office and photo work, and the String Orchestra.
first_visit_tips: Volunteers must be 16 or older; the form has options for younger people.
Start the PA child abuse, PA State Police and FBI clearances early; the FBI check applies if you lived outside Pennsylvania in the last ten years.
Have a driver's license ready for the form, and your own car if you will transport instruments.
Ask about lessons or residencies by email or phone before you visit the office at 1700 Market Street, Suite 1005.

records.notes: The public way into lessons and residencies is a staff contact; no class schedule, prices or public enrollment steps are published. Clearance names come from the volunteer page, which does not use the term Act 153, so act153_clearances is left out. Youth volunteer options exist for under 18s on the form. Training and time commitment are not stated. The homepage links an Events and News section with no items visible on the page read, so no dated news was found. The copyright year 2026 was not used as evidence.

records.name: Nationalities Service Center
records.summary: A more than 100-year-old group that helps immigrants and refugees in Greater Philadelphia with English classes, legal help, health services and youth programs. Volunteers help with classes, the food pantry, events and home setup for newly arrived refugees.
records.what_you_do: Take an in-person English class, or volunteer to teach English, help the food pantry, help at events, or set up homes for newly arrived refugees. Groups from schools, congregations or businesses can also help with home setup and donation drives.

schedule.text: English classes run in 10-week sessions on Mondays and Wednesdays, 10 am to 12 pm. Volunteer shifts can be one time or ongoing.

cost.text: English classes cost $100 for the full session, paid at registration. Volunteering is free.

access.notes: Barriers can be reported by phone, email or mail, and the group aims to reply within 14 business days. Its website works with a keyboard and with screen readers.

first_step.how: Call 215-893-8400 to ask about the next English class session, or register for a volunteer shift through the link on the volunteer page.
first_step.basis: English classes start at beginner level and volunteer roles are open to the public, but classes charge $100 per session before you start and enrollment goes through a staff contact.
first_step.what_to_expect: English classes meet in person at the Arch Street office on Mondays and Wednesdays from 10 am to 12 pm for 10 weeks. Students are placed in one of six levels from beginner to advanced, and the page does not explain how placement works. The fee is $100 for the session and is paid when you register.
first_visit_tips: Ask how placement works and what to bring when you call, since the course page does not say.
Plan for the $100 session fee, which is paid at registration.
Fall 2026 classes started October 5, 2026, so ask when the next session begins.
Ask about building entry, elevators and parking before you come, since the site does not describe the building.

records.notes: Volunteer coordinator contacts on the volunteer page: volunteers@nscphila.org and (267) 540-8511; volunteer sign-up runs through an outside volunteer platform linked from that page. The English class instructor's contact is on the course page and is not recorded here. The 100-year history in the summary is carried from tier 1 and is not on the pages read. Course page dates: registration opened September 21, 2026, and classes started October 5, 2026. Building access, wheelchair access, interpreters and placement method are not described on the pages read. Accessibility page has no building details.

records.name: Neighborhood Bike Works
records.summary: A community bike shop that teaches young people to repair bikes and lets them earn a bike by finishing a program. It also runs group rides for youth and open shop nights for adults.
records.what_you_do: Youth ages 8 to 18 learn repair by fixing a donated bike in Earn-a-Bike, or join Ride Club for after-school group rides. Adults can walk in to work on their own bikes with the shop's stands and tools, or take a four-week adult repair class.

schedule.text: Youth programs meet Monday to Thursday, 4 to 6 pm, in sessions. Adults can drop in on Tuesday, Thursday and Friday afternoons, on Tuesday and Thursday evenings for Bike Church, and on Wednesday evenings at a shift limited to women, trans and nonbinary people.

cost.text: Youth classes are free, with a $25 deposit refunded when the student finishes. Bike Church asks for a donation. The adult four-week repair class costs $175.

requirements.gear: Bikes and helmets can be provided for Ride Club.

first_step.how: Fill in the Youth Programs Interest Form on the group's website, then sign up for the next Earn-a-Bike or Ride Club session.
first_step.basis: Earn-a-Bike teaches repair from the start for ages 8 to 18 and begins with an interest form, and the adult Bike Church takes walk-ins with no reservation; Ride Club needs riding skill first.
first_step.what_to_expect: Earn-a-Bike and Ride Club meet two afternoons a week, Monday and Wednesday or Tuesday and Thursday, from 4 to 6 pm. Adults can walk in to Bike Church on Tuesday or Thursday evenings, where volunteers help diagnose and fix problems on your own bike.
first_visit_tips: Ride Club asks that you can ride 20 minutes without a stop, and students need 75% attendance to graduate.
Bring the bike you want to work on to an adult open shop night.
The Saturday Youth Drop-In is for program graduates, so start with the interest form.
The shop is at 3939 Lancaster Avenue, zip 19104. The site does not give transit or parking details.

records.notes: Corrections to tier 1: the Saturday open shop is a Youth Drop-In for program graduates only, not for all youth; the $25 class deposit is refundable; the minimum age of 8 covers youth programs, and adult shifts are 18 and up. The group file lists a staff email (a different address from the one the group publishes); the youth page publishes info@ and that is recorded here, so the file may need a check. The bike-shop page has a heading that reads Mel's Community Bike Shop; that is not used as a name. Bike Church is described as donation based in one place and as free in another, so the donation wording is used. The adult repair class dates on the page have no year and are not recorded. The Bicycle Coalition youth team is named on the youth page with no link, so it is not logged as a lead.

records.name: Network for New Music
records.summary: A Philadelphia ensemble that performs and commissions new contemporary music. It also runs school workshops and a yearly double bass ensemble that includes hobbyist players.
records.what_you_do: Attend concerts in the season, or join the yearly double bass performance, which includes professional, student and hobbyist players and has a call for paid bassists. The group also takes gifts to its annual fund and commissioning fund.

schedule.text: Concerts run in a yearly season listed on the group's website.

cost.text: Ticket prices are not shown on the pages read.

first_step.how: Choose a program from the current season on the group's website and check its listing for tickets.
first_step.basis: Concerts are open to the public and listed by season, which is a clear way in, though the site shows no path beyond attending.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site lists programs by name, such as Crossfade and Schoenberg in Hi-Fi, without dates on the pages read. It does not say how long a concert runs or what tickets cost. The double bass call is a separate project with paid positions.
first_visit_tips: Look for the program you want on the season page before you buy anything.
If you play double bass, ask about the yearly ensemble by email through the education contact on the education page.
Check the ticket listing for the price, since the site does not show it on the pages read.

records.notes: No exact tag exists for a new music ensemble. community_band is kept as the closest fit because the double bass project takes hobbyist players. The education page mostly serves school classrooms and university composers; its workshop list prices are for schools and are not recorded. The office address 6757 Greene St comes from the IRS record and the Cultural Fund listing, not the group's own site, which shows no office address. The 2026 to 2027 season name appears only in the site menu, with no dated item, so status stays probably_active and last_sign_of_life is not set. The site's 2025 to 2026 season thank-you has no date.

records.name: New Paradise Laboratories
records.summary: A theater company, active since 1996, that makes its own performance projects. Its site shows photos and videos of past work and lists no current show on the pages read.
records.what_you_do: Watch for the next show or project, then buy a ticket when one is announced. The site does not list volunteer roles, classes or youth programs.

schedule.text: Shows are announced one at a time, and no regular class or season is listed on the site.

cost.text: Ticket prices are not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Follow the company on Facebook or Instagram, or email it to ask how to hear about new shows, then buy a ticket when a show is announced.
first_step.basis: Shows are announced one at a time, and the site shows no sign-up, class or open-door path for newcomers.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a show runs, where it is staged, or what it costs, so a first visit depends on the show that is announced. The company's social media pages and email are the only ways to reach it that the site shows.
first_visit_tips: Ask by email how to get notice of new shows, since the site does not describe a mailing list.
Look up the venue when a show is announced, because the site gives no address.
Check the ticket price before you go, since none is shown on the site.

records.notes: Only the homepage could be read. The Recent Projects page returned a 404 at the path tried, and no show, class, ticket or volunteer page was found. The group's site shows no street address, so none is recorded. Image folder years (2021 and 2024) are upload dates, not event dates, and were not used. Status probably_active rests only on a working site with no dates; re-check when a show is announced. Verdict publish is held loosely because no current public event is visible.
